Commentary.Commentary: So, Kane Williamson hurt his hamstring and will take no further part in this game. Tim Southee to captain his side. The players are in the middle for the chase. Tim Southee to bowl first..
...THE CHASE...

Allen scored a quick fifty but New Zealand lost wickets at regular intervals which hampered their momentum a bit. New Zealand in the last five overs failed to go big and have ended under 200. Pakistan were okay with the ball. They didn't make the most of the swing available at the start and allowed the Kiwi batters to get some easy runs. However, Pakistan will be confident to chase this down. A good start is required for them. Can the openers lay the foundation for others to chase it down? Let's find out.

Excellent fightback from Pakistan in the last phase and they have given themselves a real chance to win this game. Anything under 200 and Pakistan were going to be in this game. New Zealand will be disappointed with the score, knowing they were in such a commanding position for a long period. Finn Allen gave a blistering start and he along with Kane Williamson added over 50 runs. The skipper though during the halfway mark got injured out and is still unknown if he will take the field.
A single to end the innings. Fuller and outside off. Southee knocks it to cover for a single. New Zealand end with 194 for 9.

It was not a dream start to Shaheen Afridi’s captaincy career as Pakistan were convincingly beaten by the hosts in the first match. Pakistan were in the game for a while but the middle order collapsed at the wrong time. Afridi will not only try to rectify their batting but their continues fielding woes was on show as well which cost them quite a few runs along with a couple of bowlers conceding more than 50 runs.
...Match Day...

We're in for a thriller as New Zealand and Pakistan face off in the second T20I at Seddon Park in Hamilton! The Black Caps will be looking to ride the momentum from their commanding win in the first match. The Kiwi batters showcased their firepower, with Finn Allen scoring a quick 34, Kane Williamson anchoring with a stylish 57, and Daryl Mitchell exploding for a sensational 61, propelling New Zealand to a steep total of 226. Every single cricket fan doesn't matter from which geography, was simply awe-struck by such clean hitting. Despite Shaheen Afridi and debutant Abbas Afridi's impressive 3-fers, they couldn't prevent the daunting total. In reply, Pakistan lost early wickets. Saim Ayub and Mohammad Rizwan did provide explosive initiation up the order but perished sooner. Babar Azam's blazing 57 was the biggest highlight for them. However, the Kiwi veteran Tim Southee's 4-wicket haul, making him the first bowler with 150 T20I wickets, led to Pakistan's middle-order collapse, as Pakistan got bundled up on 180. The Blackcaps emerged as deserved 46-run victors but Pakistan will be keen to bounce back strongly in Hamilton. When New Zealand and Pakistan clashed at picturesque Seddon Park previously, the Kiwis dominated with a dominating 9-wicket victory. The Kiwis have a strong track record at this venue, losing only 2 of their last 10 matches. New Zealand's batting order is firing on all cylinders and their bowling artillery didn't disappoint either. They will aim to continue their home dominance. The visitors will have to up their game in all departments, especially in preventing any further fielding mishaps. With home advantage on their side, the Kiwis will be eager to seize a 2-0 lead, while Pakistan will be hungry for a comeback.
